AE+SE positioned Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private with a proposed POC to run parity benchmarks and a routing fall-back plan.

transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-10-07
- Time: 15:00 UTC
- Duration: 58 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan Meyers (Redwood AE), Riya Patel (Redwood SE), Luis Ortega (CTO - Zenwave), Maya Chen (Platform Eng), Samir Bose (ML Eng)

Auto-generated Summary (may be imperfect):
Zenwave is exploring exit from OpenAI + hybrid on-prem vLLM to a consistent inference platform. Primary drivers: predictable unit economics, private data control for PII, and fewer operational headaches at scale. Team wants to run parity evals on their prompt sets.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro, I'm Jordan with Redwood, ae for your region, Riya is my solutions engineer.
[00:14] Luis: thanks Jordan. we (Zenwave) run user-facing assistants across healthcare forms so data residency and PII are huge. right now we use OpenAI for most prod traffic and vLLM for on-prem research.
[00:28] Riya: great, that mix is common. curious - when you say vLLM on-prem, is that full production or just experiments?
[00:37] Samir: mostly experiments and some batch jobs. latency sensitive stuff hits OpenAI because it's simpler to scale, but costs are spiking. also we have a dedicated infra team but they'd prefer fewer home-grown patches.
[00:52] Maya: plus compliance. our legal team wants stronger audit trails and KMS integration for customer data. OpenAI has some enterprise SLAs but the VPC/on-prem story we want is clearer.
[01:08] Jordan: understood. quick outline today: we want to map your current stack, discuss Redwood hosting options - hosted api, dedicated reserved capacity, or private VPC/on-prem - and propose a POC scope for parity checks.
[01:23] Luis: perfect. what are the tradeoffs re: latency vs cost across those modes?
[01:29] Riya: short answer: hosted is fastest to ship — lower ramp and managed scale; dedicated gives predictable throughput and cost at commit levels; private gives max data control but requires more ops on your side. latency depends on model choice and placement. if you keep traffic regional to our hosted infra latency often matches or beats external API calls depending on network egress.
[01:48] Samir: about models — we currently use GPT-like models from OpenAI and fine-tuned Anthropic for safety-critical flows. For on-prem we run an MPT variant on vLLM and we use TGI for some proprietary kernels. any compatibility gotchas?
[02:06] Riya: we support a wide catalog and can run most transformer models; runtime differences surface mostly around tokenizer mismatches, kv-cache behavior and custom ops TGI compiles. our onboarding includes a compatibility pass. sometimes naming of special tokens or padding conventions cause small diffs, we flag those in early parity tests.
[02:30] Luis: curious about kv cache — our long-context flows rely heavily on KV reuse. we've seen vLLM implementations with differences in cache invalidation that change outputs.
[02:40] Riya: yes KV semantics matter. Redwood's runtime preserves deterministic KV eviction semantics and offers prefix caching. during the POC we instrument token-level tracing so you can compare per-step hidden states and cache hits.
[02:56] Maya: what's the path for data residency? we can't send raw PII to hosted for a subset of customers.
[03:03] Jordan: options: keep most traffic on hosted for cost-sensitive flows but route PII-tagged requests to private deployment in your VPC, or use Dedicated with tenant isolation and bring-your-own-KMS. We also have network-level routing policies and can do in-flight redaction at the app layer.
[03:21] Samir: do you support HSM/KMS like AWS KMS or customer HSM?
[03:26] Riya: yes, we integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and can support customer-managed HSM through private deployment. audit logs include per-request key usage and we can push logs to your SIEM.
[03:40] Luis: benchmark talk — we need to ensure output quality parity first. our legal team won't approve unless generation is within acceptable delta of our current models. what's typical for Redwood parity projects?
[03:53] Jordan: most customers run a 2-week parity POC: you provide prompts and evals, we run hosted + dedicated + private if needed, and produce quality metrics (ROUGE/BLEU where relevant, but more often we run pairwise human evals and embed-similarity metrics).
[04:11] Maya: pairwise human evals — do you support our internal annotators or do you help source evaluators?
[04:17] Riya: we can run the automated metrics and host the platform for your annotators to do blind evals. we also offer optional annotation services for a fee.
[04:29] Samir: regarding TGI — we rely on custom kernels. will Redwood be able to run our TGI-compiled weights or is there a conversion step?
[04:38] Riya: we generally can run the weights but sometimes need to recompile kernels; we have a conversion toolchain for TGI/vLLM artifacts. performance can vary, and we surface optimized quantization profiles. if you have proprietary ops we may need engineering time.
[04:54] Luis: costs — how do you price POC and then recurring?
[04:58] Jordan: POC pricing is typically a discounted usage bucket plus engineering hours if we need custom connector work. recurring: hosted is usage-based, dedicated is committed capacity (monthly), private is platform fee plus support. we'll share a tailored quote after we define throughput and model mix.
[05:14] Luis: okay. our traffic profile: peak 600 rps across several regions, typical prompt median tokens 350, tail to 2k for some transcripts.
[05:25] Riya: good data point. with that tail you'd want to look at batching strategies carefully; continuous batching helps but for low-latency sub-200ms paths we isolate a small pool of low-latency nodes.
[05:40] Samir: about burst capacity — any autoscale limits for dedicated?
[05:43] Jordan: dedicated supports configurable burst, and you can set fallback policies to hosted for excess, or queue with SLA-aware tails.
[05:53] Maya: security checklist — SOC2, SSO/SAML, RBAC, tenant isolation, data retention windows?
[05:59] Riya: Redwood has SOC2, supports SAML/SSO, SCIM for provisioning, role-based access controls, and retention policies. private deployments let you manage retention more strictly. we have audit log exports and can integrate with your SIEM.
[06:16] Luis: any customers in healthcare who used private deployment?
[06:19] Jordan: yes, a few. we can share redacted case studies and compliance checklist. I'll attach them after the call.
[06:26] Samir: technical deep dive request — we want a follow-up with your infra folks to understand kernel selection, quantization tradeoffs and KV design, also a bench run on our MPT/TGI stacks.
[06:38] Riya: noted. we usually have a 90-minute SE deep dive for that and then run a controlled bench with your artifacts.
[06:46] Luis: timeline — legal expects a vendor recommendation by end of Q4. can that happen?
[06:50] Jordan: yes, with a 2-week POC starting as early as mid-October we can get results to feed procurement by late November.
[06:58] Maya: network detail — we're peered in us-east and eu-west, some traffic originates in APAC. can Redwood host in those regions?
[07:06] Riya: hosted infra covers major regions and we can deploy private stacks within your VPC in those regions.
[07:14] Samir: small nit — tokenization differences sometimes cause scoring gaps. do you provide a tokenizer parity check?
[07:21] Riya: yes, tokenizer parity is step one: we run tokenization diff tools to surface off-by-one sequences, byte-level diffs and advise small prompt tweaks or tokenizer configs.
[07:33] Speaker Unknown: yeah uh, we also saw some mismatch in stop token handling between TGI and other runtimes — would Redwood respect model stop tokens?
[07:43] Riya: we follow model-specified stop tokens, but if you use application-side stopping we can instrument both to verify behavior.
[07:52] Luis: for the POC, what metrics do you deliver? beyond latency and token cost.
[07:58] Jordan: we'll deliver: latency P50/P90/P99, per-token cost breakdown, model quality metrics (pairwise, embedding similarity), cache hit rates, and a regression diff report on outputs with examples.
[08:12] Maya: any guidance on quantization? we are exploring 4-bit for cost savings but worried about accuracy hit on safety-critical flows.
[08:21] Riya: quantization profiles are workload dependent. we recommend rolling quantization on non-critical traffic first and measuring with your evals. Redwood Optimize can suggest profiles based on prompt distributions.
[08:33] Samir: curious — what about reproducibility? some of our audit requirements ask for deterministic seeds and reproducible outputs for a given model version.
[08:42] Riya: we support pinned model versions and deterministic sampling modes. full determinism across different runtimes is tricky if sampling differs, but we provide seeding and recommend fixed sampling for auditable outputs.
[08:59] Jordan: do you have any red lines that would rule out hosted entirely?
[09:03] Luis: for HIPAA-level PII we likely require private or a VPC/Dedicated arrangement with customer-managed KMS. Also legal cares about egress to third-party vendors.
[09:14] Jordan: understood. we can architect a mixed routing plan where sensitive requests hit private nodes in your VPC and everything else is served by hosted.
[09:23] Maya: any SLA differences between dedicated and private?
[09:26] Riya: dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency targets. private SLAs are part of the enterprise package and depend on the support tier.
[09:34] Samir: follow-up: can you export token-level logs for billing reconciliation?
[09:38] Jordan: yes we have token-level cost breakdowns and can stream detailed logs into your logging infrastructure, redacted as needed.
[09:47] Luis: example shared artifacts?
[09:49] Jordan: I'll share: 1) POC template + checklist (link), 2) hosting comparison matrix, 3) past healthcare case study, 4) benchmark plan spreadsheet. (Recorded note: links will be posted in CRM).
[10:03] Maya: we need to know the ramp for engineering support during POC — how much SE time?
[10:08] Riya: typically 8-16 hours across discovery and setup, and additional 16-40 hours if we need custom conversion or kernel work. we'll estimate after we see artifacts.
[10:20] Samir: can we bring our on-prem vLLM into Redwood private? or do we have to move weights?
[10:27] Riya: private deployments can run in your environment; you can bring existing containers/weights. sometimes we recommend using our runtime for stability and optimizations, but hybrid approaches are supported.
[10:40] Luis: are there any differences in model versioning behavior when you pin versions? we need to be able to roll back quickly.
[10:46] Riya: Redwood supports model version pinning, canary rollouts and automatic fallback to pinned safe models. rollbacks are controlled via the control plane.
[11:00] Jordan: ok let's recap next steps real quick.
[11:03] Jordan: Jordan to share POC template, hosting matrix and pricing. Riya to produce vLLM/TGI conversion notes and a bench plan. Maya to provide prompt corpus and traffic profile. Also schedule an SE deep dive.
[11:18] Luis: sounds good. quick question — competitor lock-in: how easy to exit Redwood later?
[11:24] Riya: we export models and logs, and we support standardized model artifact formats. we emphasize customer data portability in contracts.
[11:34] Maya: pragmatic question — what's the expected token price delta vs current OpenAI contract?
[11:39] Jordan: depends on volume and model mix; many customers see 20-50% per-token savings when using dedicated or optimized quantized flows. we'll include estimated numbers in the quote.
[11:54] Samir: any gotchas you usually see in migrations?
[11:58] Riya: tokenization, stop tokens, and subtle sampling differences in safety filters. also operational edge cases: KV cache warmups, and latency tail management. doing a thorough parity test catches most issues.
[12:17] Luis: ok thanks. are we agreed to proceed to share artifacts and aim for a mid-Oct start?
[12:23] Maya: yes; legal will still want a compliance questionnaire but we can start the tech POC while that proceeds.
[12:29] Jordan: perfect. I'll follow up after the call with meeting notes and links to the docs.
[12:35] Luis: thanks all.
[12:37] End of recording.
